justification: Version 2 raises only the paired-ratio timing floor, from 1.10 to 1.25, through the change procedure of version 1 (budget-policy.v1.json, SHA-256 edf9fde4361dcfaa3e5436a9d356aa4fdb6655547f0661e15665cf8fbb490e6c). Cause: CE-01.1 (#44, PR #106 at 4fddcdd) adds an always-on capability: the compiler checks every emitted CSS feature against the browser targets, and runs that check in advisory mode, producing warnings, when no targets are configured. Measured cost: gated in release mode against the frozen alpha1 control under version 1, the candidate passes every memory, deterministic and identity budget and fails five paired timing budgets, at median ratios of x1.118 to x1.166: alpha1-valid-fixture full.toDiagnosticsMs 1.118; ce-corpus full.totalMs 1.139; ce-corpus full.toDiagnosticsMs 1.145; ce-corpus incremental.local-style.toDiagnosticsMs 1.130; synthetic-c10000 incremental.token-value.toDiagnosticsMs 1.166 (interval 1.067 to 1.333). Four more were inconclusive under version 1, with intervals straddling the limit or a noisy control: alpha1-valid-fixture full.totalMs (median 1.095), and synthetic-c10000 compiler.importMs, incremental.local-style.toDiagnosticsMs and incremental.token-value.totalMs, each on 5 pairs. Profiles attribute the difference to the inherent cost of checking every feature: about 24 ms of the roughly 190 ms cold ce-corpus validation, and about 0.4 ms per incremental edit. CE-01.1 is not redesigned to hide that cost. The floor is cumulative against alpha1 for the whole core-evolution epic, not per lot: every later candidate is still compared with the unchanged alpha1 artifact, so CE-01.1 alone already uses up to about 0.17 of the 0.25 allowance. The remaining headroom is deliberately small, and later lots must not assume more; a further increase needs its own policy version and justification. Recovery of this cost is owned by CE-12.3 (#76). The version 2 baseline runs (alpha1-v2-sk-b2 and alpha1-v2-sk-b3) were measured on a different host from version 1 (AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, recorded in the budgets baseline environment). Paired timing ratios are relative to the interleaved alpha1 control; the absolute memory limits derive from that host's alpha1 medians and are bound to that measurement host, in particular the two synthetic-c10000 peak-RSS cells, which version 2 derives as absolute limits because their coefficient of variation there is about 0.5%. A gate run measured on another host is outside the contract of version 2. On the version 1 host, c10000 peak RSS of the identical artifact is bimodal (about 1.05 GB or about 2.3 GB, documented with version 1); that is a property of that host, not a defect of version 2. Every other rule is unchanged: the runtime and memory floors, the memory rule, deterministic growth, identity, budgeted metrics, workloads, noise ceiling, minimum pairs and rounding. The budgets are re-derived from a new comparable baseline run of the unchanged alpha1 artifact, and every budget whose derived limit loosens relative to version 1 is listed in relaxations.

pairedRatio.applies: timing and runtime metrics, and memory cells whose baseline CV exceeds memory.maxCv

comparison: Run tools/baselines/measure.mjs with the final plan and both --epoch alpha1=<alpha1 closure> and --epoch <candidate>=<candidate closure> on one machine (--require-quiet is optional). budgets.mjs gate pairs each candidate sample with the adjacent alpha1 sample of the same round, applies the paired-ratio, absolute-memory, deterministic and identity budgets, requires alpha1 to reproduce its frozen deterministic outputs, and lists unknown metrics. Verdicts: pass only when every budget passes; fail on any failing budget, workload-record mismatch, altered alpha1 tarball or policy-chain problem; inconclusive when the run lacks the interleaved control, has too few pairs, exceeds a noise ceiling or cannot resolve a limit; incomplete when a budgeted metric was not run.

changePolicy: budgets.v2.json is generated by `node tools/baselines/budgets.mjs freeze` from this policy and the committed baseline results, and is never edited by hand; rerunning the same freeze command with this policy and the referenced results must reproduce it byte for byte.

Committed policy, budgets, workloads, derivation and baseline result files are immutable; `budgets.mjs gate` compares the budgets file with the version of the commit that added it and fails on any difference.

Changing a threshold, metric set or workload requires a new budget-policy.vN.json and budgets.vN.json (N incremented), a justification, a predecessor reference by path and SHA-256, and a new comparable baseline run of the unchanged alpha1 artifact; reusing an old result file is rejected.
Every budget loosened or removed relative to the predecessor must be listed in `relaxations` with its own justification; an unknown metric may only leave the unknown list by gaining a budget.

No release may pass against a weakened budget retroactively: the gate evaluates the budgets version current at the evaluated commit, fails on any policy-chain problem, and never reports inconclusive or incomplete as pass.
